(By Sri Lakshminarayana, Adv.)
 SCCH.13 3 MVC.3806/2020  JUDGMENT
This petition under Sec.166 of M.V.Act., is filed claiming compensation of Rs.21,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the original claimant Muniraju in a Road traffic accident.

Thereafter, during pendency of petition, Petitioner Muniraju died and his LRs came on record and they prayed for the compensation of 21,00,000/- for death of Muniraju due to the accidental injuries.
2.

The brief facts of the case are that on 20-09- 2020 at around 12.30 p.m., Muniraju was riding his two-wheeler bearing No.KA-01-2864 from Hunasaghattapalya towards Nelamangala and when he reached Kunigal - Nelamangala NH 75 Road, near Bavikere Cross, opposite to Mangala Granites,
Nelamangala Taluk, at that time, the driver of Car bearing No.KA-02-MH-371 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) drove the same with high speed and in a rash & negligent manner and dashed against the two-wheeler and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, Muniraju sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was taken to Mathrusree Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and due to accidental injuries he could not recovered, he was mentally and physically disturbed and died on 19.01.2021 by taking poison.
The Petitioners have spent more than .2,50,000/- towards medical expenses, food and nourishment, conveyances, attendant charges and other incidental charges, funeral and obsequies expenses.
The accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
3. Prior to the accident, Muniraju was hale and healthy, aged 50 years and earning his livelihood by doing agriculture and dairy farming and earning .21,000/- p.m.
The Petitioners are the LRs of the deceased and they were depending on the earnings of the deceased.
Hence, they claimed compensation of .21,00,000/- from the Respondents with costs and interest from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
On the above grounds, they had prayed for allowing the petition.

sentences.text: In response to the petition notice, both the Respondents have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. Respondent No.1-who is RC owner of the offending vehicle has denied the petition averments.

He has admitted that offending vehicle belonged to him and same was insured with the Respondent No.2 and the policy was valid as on the date of accident and driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
The death of the claimant is not due to the accidental injuries.
He has denied the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle and contended that the accident has occurred due to negligence of deceased.

5. Further respondent No.1 has filed additional written statement contending that deceased Muniraju was riding the two-wheeler on national highway without valid DL, insurance and helmet and contended that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident.
Further he has contended that the offending vehicle was got repaired by spending Rs.40,000/- and damages were caused to the offending vehicle due to the rash and negligent riding of the deceased.

He has denied that Muniraju died due to the accidental injuries and contended that due to his commitment he might have taken the poison and denied that the petitioners are the LRs of deceased and prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. Respondent No.2 - insurance company has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of offending vehicle, its validity as on the date of the accident but its liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further, contended that the the driver of offending vehicle was not having valid DL.
Hence, there is violation of terms of policy.

Further, it has denied the occurrence of accident, involvement of offending vehicle, age, occupation, income, injuries sustained by Muniraju,
expenses incurred for treatment and dependency of the Petitioners.
It is also contended that the compensation claimed in the petition is highly exaggerated.

7. Further, the respondent No.2 has filed additional written statement and contended that there was no nexus between accidental injuries and death of Muniraju as he died due to suicide by taking poison therefore, the petition may be dismissed.
8. On the basis of the above pleadings, following recasted Issues are framed:-

1. Whether the Petitioners prove that death of Sri.Muniraju S/o.Muniyappa was only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing No.KA-02-MH-371 on 20-09-2020 about 12.30 p.m. near Kunigal Road, near Bavikere Cross, opposite Mangala Granite, Nelamangala, Bengaluru District ?
2. What compensation petitioners are entitled ?
3. What order ?
9. In order to prove the case, petitioner No.1(a) is examined as PW-1 and in support of their case, 3 witnesses were examined as PW-2 to 4 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 26.

By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above recasted Issues as under:
Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative. Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 12.
Issue No.1: After death of the petitioner, his legal representatives came on record, deceased wife examined as PW1.

In order to prove their claim, PW-1 has deposed that on 20-09-2020 at around 12.30 p.m., Muniraju was riding his two-wheeler bearing No.KA-01- 2864 from Hunasaghattapalya towards Nelamangala and when he reached Kunigal - Nelamangala NH 75 Road, near Bavikere Cross, opposite to Mangala Granites, Nelamangala Taluk, at that time, the driver of Car bearing No.KA-02-MH-371 drove the same with high speed and in a rash & negligent manner and dashed against the two-wheeler and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, Muniraju sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was taken to Mathrusree Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and due to accidental injuries he could not recovered, he was mentally and physically disturbed and died on 19.01.2021 by taking poison.

13. In support of their claim, Petitioner No.1(a) is examined as PW.1 and has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P1, FIS at Ex.P2, spot Mahazar at Ex.P.3, notice and reply at Ex.P.4 and EX.P.5, UDR with complaint at Ex.P.6, PM report at Ex.P.7, wound certificate at Ex.P.9 and charge sheet at Ex.P.10.
On perusal of wound certificate, it shows that Muniraju has sustained Segmental fracture of both bones of right forearm and segmental fracture of right femur.
Both injuries are grievous in nature.

14. During the cross-examination of PW1, the learned counsel for the Respondent has put forth the suggestion that the accident has occurred due to negligence of deceased and not on part of the driving of the offending vehicle and false case was registered against the offending vehicle.
However PW1 has denied the same.
To prove their contention, the eye witnesses to the incident were examined as PW3 and PW 4.
They have stated that the offending vehicle caused the accident and thereby Muniraju sustained injuries.
Nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW3 and 4 to disprove the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
15. To support its version the official of respondent is examined as RW1.he
has produced EX.R.2 policy.
He has reiterated the contention of its written statement.
During the cross-examination, he admitted that the policy was in force.
He has stated they are not disputed that it was negligence of the driver of the insured car.
The owner of the offending vehicle is examined as RW2.
He has reiterated the contention of his written statement During the course of cross-examination
, he admitted that the offending car sustained damages left side bonnet, bumber and radiator.

He denied Muniraju vs K.Narasimhaiah on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186146014/

sentences.text: 16. After thorough investigation IO has been filed charge sheet against offending vehicle.
Absolutely there are no contrary materials.
There are no materials to show that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident and it was not the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
All the records corroborate with the evidence of Petitioner.
Hence I hold that Muniraju had sustained injuries in a RTA due to negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
The driver of offending vehicle was negligent and it caused the injuries to Muniraju.
17. PW1 deposed that due to accidental injuries her husband/ deceased could not recovered, he was mentally and physically disturbed and thereby committed suicide on 19.01.2021.
It is stated that the accident was solely due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending motorcycle.

In order to substantiate her claim, she has produced Copy of UDR marked at Ex.P.6, True copy of PM report at Ex.P.7 and copy of death certificate marked at Ex.P.8.
18.
The learned counsel for petitioners has vehemently argued that there is nexus between the accidental injuries and death of Muniraju.
Due to accidental injuries the deceased committed suicide.
He relied upon the decisions rendered in MACA No.2138/2010 between M/s. New India Assurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Vijayan and others and (2012) 2 SCC 267 between Mohan Soni Vs. Ram Avtar Tomar and others.

sentences.text: 19. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 vehemently argued that there is no nexus between the accidental injuries and death of Muniraju.

The LRs of petitioner have not produced any documents to substantiate that due to accidental injuries, Muniraju was mentally and physically disturbed and there by he committed suicide and further he argued that the death was as a consequence of bodily injury sustained in the motor vehicle accident, his legal representatives are entitled to claim compensation towards loss of estate of the deceased person and not otherwise.
20. Keeping in view of arguments addressed by the parties, once again I have perused the material available on record.
PW1 has deposed that Muniraju was unable to perform his daily activities independently, hence he committed suicide.
During the cross-examination, she stated that he was taking treatment for his injuries till his death.
However she has not produced any documents to substantiate the same.
She has not produced any documents to substantiate that Muniraju was under depression or he was suffering from pain as such he committed suicide.
21. Dr. Srinivasa is examined as PW2.
PW2 has produced case sheet and X-rays at EX P21 and 22.
PW2 doctor admitted that at time of discharge the condition of the deceased was stable.
The deceased came his hospital twice as out patient.
Except EX P11, P16 and 21 treatment, till his death there are no other treatment taken by the deceased petitioner.
There are no medical bills either to show that he was continuously taking medicines or was under treatment.
As per EX P9 wound certificate and EX P11 discharge summary, the deceased sustained fractures to both bones of arm and right femur.
The injuries shown in the wound certificate and discharge summary are not so severe to cause death of any person.
After the discharge he was at home for more than 4 months and died on 19/1/2021.
The cause of committing suicide is not known.

No doctor has been examined to Muniraju vs K.Narasimhaiah on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186146014/
5 prove that due to accidental injuries the petitioner had gone through depression and thereby he committed suicide.

sentences.text: No documents were produced to prove that the deceased was taking treatment for depression.
In the absence of specific documents to show that he committed suicide due to accidental injuries, it cannot be held that Muniraju died due to accidental injuries.
Though the PW1 to 4 has stated accidental injuries might have contributed the death of Muniraju, there is no documentary evidence to substantiate her version.
Therefore, this tribunal has not given any importance to the oral testimony of PW1 to 4.
with due respect of decisions relied by the Lrs petitioner, the facts and circumstances of the above said are not squarely applicable to this case.
22. The LRs of Petitioners have failed to prove the nexus between the accidental injuries and the death of original claimant.
Further, during the course of cross-examination, the PW3 and 4 have stated that they did not know the cause and reason of death of the petitioner.
PW-1 has not proved to be bed ridden or suffering with severe complications till his death or due to accidental injuries the petitioner had committed suicide.
In the present case as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1, the injured has not suffered any physical disability nor he was under any treatment at the time of his death.
As I have already discussed that there is no material to show that the death was on account of and as a direct consequence of injuries suffered by the deceased in the motor vehicle accident.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Partly Affirmative.
23. ISSUE NO.2:

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue No, I hold that LRs of Petitioner are entitled only for the medical expenses in view of the various decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court and High Court of Karnataka.

It is relevant to note in case of ILR 1990 KAR 4300 between Kannamma V/s Deputy General Manager wherein the Hon'ble High Court has held that death was on account of and as a direct consequence of the injury suffered by the deceased in the motor vehicle accident.
Under such circumstances, the claimants are entitled for compensation towards hospitalization and medical expenses only and not for loss of estate.

24. In the present case the Petitioners have produced the medical bills at Ex.P.16 for Rs.1,74,850/-.Hence, Petitioner is awarded compensation of .1,74,850/- towards Medical Expenses.
25. Liability:
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Respondent No.1 being the owner and the Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.
However, Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
26. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to the above Issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioners

are awarded compensation of .1,74,850/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
